pr_body:
Connection cleanup is performed not only when BT_CONN_DISCONNECTED, but also when BT_CONN_DISCONNECTING and BT_CONN_DISCONNECT_COMPLETE. In addition  send_buf() function can return -ENOTCONN error code - the handling was added. The fix has been tested on our side and it fixes the issue.

Fixes #63217

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Host: bt_conn_process_tx() does not release TX buffers when connection state is BT_CONN_DISCONNECT_COMPLETE
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
We have a peripheral BLE device based on Zephyr RTOS and another central one is based on iOS (iPhone mobile app).
The central sends a write request command (), and without waiting for the response drops the connection. This is the trace:

2122	14.507	Master_0xaf9a84ad	LE 2M	ATT	9	29763µs	0	0	False	51	Sent Write Request, Handle: 0x0013 (Unknown: Unknown: Client Characteristic Configuration)
2123	14.507	Slave_0xaf9a84ad	LE 2M	LE LL	0	149µs	0	1	False	51	Empty PDU
2124	14.537	Master_0xaf9a84ad	LE 2M	LE LL	2	29727µs	1	1	False	52	Control Opcode: LL_TERMINATE_IND
2125	14.537	Slave_0xaf9a84ad	LE 2M	LE LL	0	149µs	1	0	False	52	Empty PDU

On the peripheral side (Zephyr), the BLE host processes the write request command, creates a write response frame, and stores it in the TX queue. It looks like there is a timing or connection state machine issue, resulting in not releasing the net buffer (write response).

In the function bt_conn_process_tx() a connection is cleaned up only when the state is BT_CONN_DISCONNECTED. In our case sometimes this function is called when the state is BT_CONN_DISCONNECT_COMPLETE. In such a scenario the connection is not cleaned up, the function tries to process buffer from the TX queue, and send_buf() returns -128 (disconnected). With this error code, the function simply returns, leaving the buffer in the TX queue.  In such a situation buffer with 'write response' is not released, and finally, acl_tx_pool can be left empty making new connections unusable.

To investigate the problem I added an additional log to bt_conn_process_tx() function:
```
void bt_conn_process_tx(struct bt_conn *conn)
{
	struct net_buf *buf;
	int err;

	LOG_DBG("conn %p", conn);

	if (conn->state == BT_CONN_DISCONNECTED &&
	    atomic_test_and_clear_bit(conn->flags, BT_CONN_CLEANUP)) {
		LOG_DBG("handle %u disconnected - cleaning up", conn->handle);
		conn_cleanup(conn);
		return;
	}

	/* Get next ACL packet for connection. The buffer will only get dequeued
	 * if there is a free controller buffer to put it in.
	 *
	 * Important: no operations should be done on `buf` until it is properly
	 * dequeued from the FIFO, using the `net_buf_get()` API.
	 */
	buf = k_fifo_peek_head(&conn->tx_queue);
	BT_ASSERT(buf);

	/* Since we used `peek`, the queue still owns the reference to the
	 * buffer, so we need to take an explicit additional reference here.
	 */
	buf = net_buf_ref(buf);
	err = send_buf(conn, buf);
	net_buf_unref(buf);

	LOG_INF("bt_conn_process_tx(): send_buf() -> %d, conn->state -> %d", err, conn->state);
	if (err  == -EIO) {
		struct bt_conn_tx *tx = tx_data(buf)->tx;
```

And from time to time I can see this is the trace:
I: bt_conn_process_tx(): send_buf() -> -128, conn->state -> 1

**To Reproduce**
The problem was discovered on STM32WB55RG Nucleo. It is hard to reproduce it as this is a kind of timing issue. To reproduce it is required to simulate a call of bt_conn_process_tx() when the connection state is BT_CONN_DISCONNECT_COMPLETE.

**Expected behavior**
Buffers from conn->tx_queue should always be properly released.

**Impact**
When all buffers from acl_tx_pool have been used but not freed, even if the BLE connection can be opened it cannot be used to communicate over GATT.

**Logs and console output**
I: bt_l2cap_create_pdu_timeout():644: pool 0x20012824 size 526
I: allocated buf 0x2000af58
I: bt_ipm_send():393: buf 0x2000af58 ref 2 pool_id 0 frags (nil)
I: bt_conn_process_tx():941: buf 0x2000af58 ref 1 pool_id 0 frags (nil)
I: bt_conn_process_tx(): send_buf() -> 0, conn->state -> 7
I: bt_l2cap_create_pdu_timeout():644: pool 0x20012824 size 526
I: allocated buf 0x2000af58
D: CCC is being written from connection 0x20002378, attribute 0x200002dc, value 0
I: GATT unsubscribed so the connection is being closed.
D: CCC notify - attribute 0x200002dc, value 0
I: bt_conn_process_tx():941: buf 0x2000af58 ref 2 pool_id 0 frags (nil)
I: bt_conn_process_tx(): send_buf() -> -128, conn->state -> 1
D: Disconnected (reason 19)


**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux, mobile application acting as a central on iPhone 12 mini, iOS 16.6.1
 - Zephyr SDK 0.15.1
 - Zephyr 3.4

**Additional context**

@theob-pro I had something urgent in the meantime, but I am going to create PR today.

So here's my analysis:
Starting from when the host receives the `DISCONNECT_COMPLETE` event.
- driver calls [`bt_recv`](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/bluetooth/host/hci_core.c#L3763)
- `bt_recv` processes the disconnect event [immediately](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/bluetooth/host/hci_core.c#L3788) *and* puts it [in the event RX queue](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/bluetooth/host/hci_core.c#L3792)
- `hci_disconn_complete_prio` [sets the state](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/bluetooth/host/hci_core.c#L839) to `BT_CONN_DISCONNECT_COMPLETE`
- `bt_conn_process_tx` runs, [tries](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/bluetooth/host/conn.c#L926) and fails to send the buffer. As you said, the buf is not popped from the queue. **This can end up leaking the buffers/metadata** because we don't check for disconnected before [popping the buf from the queue](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/bluetooth/host/conn.c#L681)
- `send_buf` returns, `buf` still has one ref. Maybe it's still in the queue, maybe not (if was last fragment or not)
- `hci_disconn_complete` runs, puts the conn into [BT_CONN_DISCONNECTED](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/bluetooth/host/hci_core.c#L863)
- this transition [sets the `BT_CONN_CLEANUP` bit](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/bluetooth/host/conn.c#L1105)
- `bt_conn_process_tx` runs again, this time the stars are aligned (right bit and conn state) and [conn_cleanup](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/bluetooth/host/conn.c#L909) is called

So I think this is correct, you did find a leak, thanks! I'll approve the PR.

Regarding
> Is the transition from BT_CONN_CONNECTED to BT_CONN_DISCONNECT_COMPLETE proper

I don't have anymore insight than you on this, but it points to a commit addressing priority in handling the disconnected event.

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/8a32c2d96705559f09327b814171ab7e89786b60

Isn't this already being done in 
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/bluetooth/host/conn.c#L643-L656

@jori-nordic What should we do with this PR? 

It may sound like it's fixing an issue, but it also sounds like that the fix here already exist and has just been moved, so to me it doesn't seem to actually change anything.

I'll have another look at the explanation (next week) and report back.

Sometimes, fixes like these are impossible to test for in bsim upstream, as the ZLL is not compatible with `BT_RECV_WORKQ_SYS` and `BT_RECV_WORKQ_BT`. These two options can lead to a very different scheduling pattern, highlighting issues like this one.

Instead of singling out "problematic" error codes, we could only check for the cases where we want to keep the buffer in the queue, E.g. -EAGAIN.
